Entry point prototypes, call sequences and runtime error behaviour beyond header layouts and flag values are not shown.
Packet path semantics, verdict handling and connection tracking object lifetime beyond attribute identifiers are not shown.

findings.text: The forwarding information base expression is described by an attribute family that separates an unspecified value from a destination register holder and a result selector and a flag word bounded by a public maximum. The result selector distinguishes output interface index from output interface name from address type. The flag word provides independent single bit requests for source lookup and destination lookup and use of packet mark and restriction to input interface and restriction to output interface and presence only check.

Connection tracking helper description carries name plus layer three protocol plus layer four protocol. Timeout description carries layer protocols plus a data blob. Expectation description carries layer protocols plus destination port plus timeout plus size. Each family starts from an unspecified value and is bounded by its own public maximum.

Stateful object types form a small numbered catalogue covering counter and quota and helper and limit and connection limit and tunnel and timeout and security mark and expectation and synproxy, with an unspecified zero value and an explicit maximum. Instances are described by table and name and type and type specific data plus use count and handle plus padding and user data, bounded by a public maximum.

Flowtables expose two independent capability bits for hardware offload and for counters, together with a mask combining them. Their description carries table and name and hook description and use count and handle plus padding and flags. The hook description carries hook number and priority and device set. Both attribute families are bounded by public maxima.

Operating system fingerprint matching carries a destination register plus time to live plus flags, where the flag set currently offers only a version request. Synproxy tuning carries maximum segment size plus window scale plus flags. Device matching distinguishes a name from a prefix. Transform lookup carries a destination register plus key selector plus direction plus security parameter number, where the key selector distinguishes IPv4 and IPv6 source and destination plus request identifier plus security parameter index.

Tracing reports identify table and chain and rule handle plus trace type plus verdict plus trace identifier, alongside link and network and transport header snapshots, input and output interface with their types, mark, protocol family, policy, padding, and connection tracking identity with direction and status and state. Trace types distinguish policy decision from chain return from rule traversal. Both enumerations are bounded by public maxima.

Number generator expressions carry destination register plus modulus plus type plus offset, with legacy set name and set identifier retained, and types distinguishing incremental from random. Tunnel handling forms a nested hierarchy where a generic tunnel carries key plus destination register plus mode, mode distinguishes none from receive from transmit, keys distinguish path from identifier, key details carry identifier and address endpoints and flags and service and lifetime and ports and options, and separate option families exist for common encapsulation variants with flags for checksum and fragmentation and sequence behaviour plus a combined mask.

Both IPv4 and IPv6 expose five hook positions ordered as pre routing then local input then forward then local output then post routing with a count of five. Priorities order defragmentation and raw and connection tracking and mangling and destination translation and filter at zero and security and source translation and helper and confirm stages, with first anchored at the most negative integer and last at the most positive integer. IPv4 also defines a socket option number for retrieving the original destination.

Netlink protocol numbers identify subsystems such as routing and user sockets and socket monitoring and logging and IPsec and security and storage and audit and lookup and connector and netfilter and device events and generic plus transport and encryption and direct memory access and crypto and shared memory communication, with one alias equating internet diagnosis to socket monitoring and a defined maximum link count. Two connection states distinguish unconnected from connected. A reserved major number is defined for networking.

The netlink address holds a family plus padding plus port identifier plus multicast group mask. The message header holds length plus type plus flags plus sequence plus port identifier. The error container holds a signed error plus an embedded message header, followed by truncated original payload and optional extended acknowledgement attributes.

The attribute header holds length plus type. A 32 bit bitfield attribute holds value plus selector. Packet info holds a group. Memory mapped request holds block size and count plus frame size and count. Memory mapped header holds status plus length plus group plus process and credential identifiers.

Attribute and policy enumerations reserve zero for unspecified or unused, list valid values, then define a double underscore maximum sentinel with the public maximum as sentinel minus one. Object and flowtable and trace and tunnel and error attribute families follow the same pattern, so validators can size tables by the public maximum.

Netlink and attribute framing align to four bytes. Header length is the aligned size of the fixed header, data starts after that, total length adds payload, space is the aligned total, iteration advances by the aligned stored length while decreasing remaining length, and validity requires remaining length to cover a header with stored length within bounds. Payload length is stored length minus space for a given inner length. Memory mapped framing reuses the same alignment.

Message flags use low bits for request and multipart and acknowledgement and echo and dump inconsistency and filtering. Higher bits are reused by context where dump versus create versus delete versus acknowledgement uses each reinterpret the same positions, with composites for dump and similar operations. Attribute types reserve the top two bits for nested and network byte order with a mask to extract the true type. Control message numbers below a threshold are reserved, with distinct values for no operation and error and dump end and overrun.

Socket options provide membership add and drop, packet info, broadcast error handling, buffer space suppression, receive and transmit ring setup, all namespace listening, membership listing, capability acknowledgement, extended acknowledgement and strict checking query. Extended errors can carry message string, offset, cookie, policy dump, missing type and missing nesting level.

Attribute policy language distinguishes invalid from flag from fixed width unsigned and signed integers of one to eight bytes plus binary and string variants and nested and nested array plus 32 bit bitfield and generic signed and unsigned integers. Policy introspection attributes describe expected type with signed and unsigned minima and maxima plus length bounds plus nested policy reference and bitfield mask plus padding and mask.

Dumps proceed as a sequence of multipart messages terminated by a done marker, with overrun signalling loss and error carrying status. Dump inconsistency and filtering flags report sequence changes and server side filtering during the walk.
Memory mapped slots progress through unused and reserved to valid, then to copy or skip dispositions as the consumer handles each frame.

The same numeric flag bits change meaning between dump and modification and deletion and acknowledgement uses, so decoding requires knowledge of the operation. Hook priority extremes reuse the integer limits for both first and last and for confirm, so ordering depends on stable tie handling. All length calculations assume four byte alignment and misaligned handling would miscompute next message and payload boundaries.

Network file system identity uses remote procedure program numbers with versions, standard and direct memory access ports, limits for data and path and name and groups, file handle and cookie sizes, a fifo device sentinel, mode bits distinguishing directory and character and block and regular and link and socket and fifo within a format mask, and a pipe directory name.
Each user visible header defines a single include guard macro that prevents multiple inclusion.
